summary: The result answers a question posed in a published paper: Kulaichev (1984) asked whether the rigid Śrī Yantra fixed by his four extra conditions on top of Huet's incidence conditions is unique. A peer-reviewed 2021 paper in Comptes Rendus Mathématique states that this uniqueness question is still open. The entry gives a certified existence-and-uniqueness theorem for this classical system of polynomial constraints, together with an interval that isolates the slope. The people likely to care work in certified computation and real algebraic geometry, computer-assisted and formally verified proof, and the mathematical history of the Śrī Yantra, which has its own line of journal papers (IJHS, The Mathematical Gazette, CRAS). The key citations check out against the sources. The account is open that the admissibility condition is the author's own choice and that the author's earlier work is an unreviewed preprint. I found no prior work that settles the question.

internal_notes.evidence: Chiodo 2021, CRAS 359, pp. 384 and 387 (full text extracted)
internal_notes.message: Checked word for word: the French text says Kulaichev 'fournit un raisonnement qui indique l'existence d'une solution et il se pose la question (toujours ouverte) de l'unicité'. The English §1.2.4 says he discusses uniqueness (p. 285), estimates the complexity, argues the answer is out of reach, and 'This problem is not considered here'. The candidate's quotes and page numbers are accurate. This is the main positive evidence that the question was posed and was regarded as open as of 2021.

Searches of the general web, arXiv-oriented queries and CRAS found no paper settling uniqueness under Kulaichev's conditions. The only related item is a Synapse pre-registration on certified enumeration (AA-Krawczyk) of well-posed subsets of the Rao (1998) constraint system. It describes a planned study with no reported results, and I could not open it (HTTP 429). It is not a prior settlement. Whether it shares an author with this candidate is unknown.

Chiodo cites C. S. Rao 1998 (IJHS 33) for systematic work on the same constrained figure, Kulaichev's own addendum listing further approximation methods from readers, and Tahta 1992, Santhi et al. 2012 and Tularam 2012 for the algebraic approach. The candidate discloses that it did not read Rao and does not mention the addendum, Tahta, Santhi et al. or Tularam. I could not reach the addendum (server refused; Scribd body truncated). Chiodo's 2021 'still open' post-dates all of these, which makes it unlikely that any of them settled the question. I have no affirmative evidence of an omission that changes the account, so this is a note, not a finding.

The full text could not be fetched (404). Search snippets confirm that the abstract says 'We study uniqueness of the solution' and confirm the quoted 12544 degree bound attributed to Kulaichev. I could not check the characterisation of numerical, residual-plot evidence for uniqueness directly. It fits the abstract and Chiodo's continued 'open'.

Uniqueness is proved under an admissibility (non-degeneracy) predicate that the submitter wrote, not one taken from Kulaichev, and the account says so. How well it matches Kulaichev's intended solution domain belongs to statement alignment and definition fidelity, not to this step. For notability it is enough that the predicate excludes only degenerate or out-of-disc figures, which is what the docstring says.
The scan has no text layer, and the page references are taken second-hand from Chiodo. The account discloses this precisely and claims no priority from it.

Paper-worthiness: Chiodo's construction result on the same figure was published in CRAS, and a certified answer to a question stated as open in that venue is plausibly a serious research note. Audience: certified computation and computational real algebraic geometry (branch-and-bound plus Krawczyk on a hard polynomial system), formal verification (fully kernel-checked computer-assisted proof without native_decide), and history of mathematics. The interest is specialist, which rules out a higher placement. The figure's cultural fame is not counted as mathematical interest.
No Comparator configuration file was supplied. The declaration list follows the Challenge order: the theorems first, then the definitions in source order.

what_would_reach_higher: Read C. S. Rao (1998, IJHS 33:203-227), the only cited prior work on the same constrained figure that the submitter has not read, and state whether it discusses uniqueness.

Cite and summarise Kulaichev's own 'Addition to Śrīyantra and its mathematical properties' and the algebraic-approach papers Chiodo lists (Tahta 1992, Math. Gazette; Santhi et al. 2012; Tularam 2012), saying in each case that it does not settle uniqueness.

Justify the admissibility predicate against Kulaichev's text, or prove that uniqueness also holds under a weaker or more literal reading, so that the result answers his question rather than a nearby variant.
Get the degree-348 minimal-polynomial and resultant-census results peer-reviewed, or formalise the minimal polynomial, to give an exact algebraic identification that others can check.
Show interest beyond the single figure, for example a reusable verified interval and Krawczyk framework for Mathlib or a general method for rigid incidence configurations, to reach a wider audience.
